arxiv-2104-09625.title: Finite Difference Nets: A Deep Recurrent Framework for Solving Evolution PDEs
arxiv-2104-09625.creator: Cheng Chang, Liu Liu, Tieyong Zeng
arxiv-2104-09625.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Cheng Chang, Liu Liu, Tieyong Zeng. There has been an arising trend of adopting deep learning methods to study partial differential equations (PDEs). In this paper, we introduce a deep recurrent framework for solving time-dependent PDEs without generating large scale data sets. We provide a new perspective, that is, a different type of architecture through exploring the possible connections between traditional numerical methods (such as finite difference schemes) and deep neural networks, particularly convolutional and fully-connected neural networks are employed.

arxiv-2109-01668.creator: Antoine Sanner, Camila González, Anirban Mukhopadhyay
arxiv-2109-01668.description: Abstract The recent achievements of Deep Learning rely on the test data being similar in distribution to the training data. In an ideal case, Deep Learning models would achieve Out-of-Distribution ( OoD ) Generalization , i.e. reliably make predictions on out-of-distribution data. Yet in practice, models usually fail to generalize well when facing a shift in distribution.

arxiv-2206-10778.title: Simultaneous extensions of metrics and ultrametrics of high power
arxiv-2206-10778.creator: Yoshito Ishiki
arxiv-2206-10778.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yoshito Ishiki. In this paper, generalized metrics mean metrics taking values in general linearly ordered Abelian groups. Using the Hahn fields, we first prove that for every generalized metric space, if the set of the Archimedean equivalence classes of the range group of the metric has an infinite decreasing sequence, then every non-empty closed subset of the space is a uniform retract of the ambient space. Next we construct simultaneous extensions of generalized metrics and ultrametrics.

arxiv-2409-01382.title: Automatic Detection of LLM-Generated Code: A Comparative Case Study of Contemporary Models Across Function and Class Granularities
arxiv-2409-01382.creator: Musfiqur Rahman, SayedHassan Khatoonabadi, Ahmad Abdellatif, Emad Shihab
arxiv-2409-01382.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Musfiqur Rahman, SayedHassan Khatoonabadi, Ahmad Abdellatif, Emad Shihab. The widespread adoption of Large Language Models (LLMs) for code generation introduces risks of incorporating suboptimal or vulnerable code into software systems. While detection mechanisms exist, they face two critical limitations: existing detectors are typically optimized for specific LLMs without systematic cross-model validation, and they operate as black boxes that identify machine-generated code without explaining the underlying structural reasons.

arxiv-2508-05320.title: Towards integrated sensors for optimized OCT with undetected photons
arxiv-2508-05320.creator: Franz Roeder, René Pollmann, Viktor Quiring, Christof Eigner, Benjamin Brecht, Christine Silberhorn
arxiv-2508-05320.description: Abstract The development of practical sensors for optical coherence tomography (OCT) with undetected photons requires miniaturization via integration. To be practical, these sensors must exhibit a large spectral bandwidth and a high brightness, which are linked to a high axial resolution and a sufficient signal to noise ratio, respectively.

pmc-11404503.title: Totally three-dimensional endoscopic mitral valve replacement in a patient with situs inversus totalis
pmc-11404503.creator: Taro Kanamori, Shota Yamanaka, Yohei Onga, Koki Maekawa, Shu Takahashi
pmc-11404503.description: Situs inversus totalis (SIT) with dextrocardia is a rare congenital anomaly that poses a surgical challenge. This case report presents the first known case of a totally 3D endoscopic mitral valve replacement (MVR), which was performed in a 75-year-old woman with SIT and severe functional mitral regurgitation.

pmc-11503361.title: Measuring the Pupillary Light Reflex Using Portable Instruments in Applied Settings
pmc-11503361.creator: Nicola S Gray, Menna Price, Jennifer Pink, Chris O’Connor, Ana Antunes, Robert J Snowden
pmc-11503361.description: The early components of the pupillary light reflex (PLR) are governed by the parasympathetic nervous system. The use of cheap, portable pupillometry devices may allow for the testing of parasympathetic-system health in field settings. We examined the reliability of two portable instruments for measuring the PLR and their sensitivity to individual differences known to modulate the PLR.

pmc-11690816.title: ADHERENCE TO INTERVENTIONS AND COGNITIVE CHANGES IN FALLEN OLDER PEOPLE: RANDOMIZED CLINICAL TRIAL
pmc-11690816.creator: Juliana Ansai, Graziele Norberto Pereira, Mariana Luiz de Melo, Mariana Ignácio Sossai, Leticia Teodoro Maciel, Mel Silva de sá, Ana Laura Oliveira Dias, Karina Gramani-Say
pmc-11690816.description: Falls are an important health challenge for older people and society. Understanding how to reduce cognitive risk factors for falls is essential to develop effective prevention strategies. The purpose of this work was to assess the impact of adherence to interventions on cognitive changes after 16 weeks in older people with a history of falls.

pmc-12269019.title: Eating habits and dietary supplement utilization according to food-related lifestyle among Korean adults: a cross-sectional study
pmc-12269019.creator: EunJung Lee, Jin A Jang, Ji-Myung Kim
pmc-12269019.description: ObjectivesThis study investigated the association between eating habits and the utilization of dietary supplements (DSs) according to food-related lifestyle (FRL) among Korean adults.MethodsThis study included a total of 300 participants (150 men and 150 women) in their 20s to 60s living in Seoul and Gyeonggi Province.

pmc-12526802.title: Gait Variability and Spatiotemporal Parameters During Emotion-Induced Walking: Assessment with Inertial Measurement Units
pmc-12526802.creator: Marvin Alvarez, Angeloh Stout, Luke Fisanick, Chuan-Fa Tang, David George Wilson, Leslie Gray, Breanne Logan, Gu Eon Kang, Kenneth Loh
pmc-12526802.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Emotion alters the way humans walk, yet most prior studies have relied on laboratory-based 3D motion capture systems. While accurate, these approaches limit translation to real-world settings and have largely focused on spatiotemporal parameters and joint motions. This study evaluated the feasibility of using inertial measurement units (IMUs) to detect emotion-related changes in gait variability as well as spatiotemporal gait parameters. Fourteen healthy young adults completed overground gait trials while wearing two ankle-mounted IMUs.

pmc-12663321.title: Associations between identity perception, symptom severity, and quality of life in adolescents with ADHD
pmc-12663321.creator: Adi Stern, Liron Lamash
pmc-12663321.description: Adolescence is a key stage for identity formation. Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a lifelong neurodevelopmental condition that significantly affects adolescents’ daily functioning and quality of life and plays an important role in shaping their identity. Illness identity refers to the extent to which a chronic diagnosis is integrated into an individual’s self-concept.

pmc-13584300.title: The associations between maternal disability and perinatal outcomes among Black and/or Hispanic women in PRAMS
pmc-13584300.creator: Sarah E Harkins, Jianfang Liu, Maya Sabatello, Veronica Barcelona
pmc-13584300.description: BackgroundWomen racialized as Black and/or Hispanic have high rates of adverse perinatal outcomes due to systemic racism. pmc-13681885.title: Periplocin targets low density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 4 and protects against osteoarthritis
pmc-13681885.creator: Jincheng Liu, Qingyang Fu, Chunlin Li, Kun Gao, Mengsi Sun, Mingyu Xu, Junfei Chen, Xu Zhai, Wencan Zhang, Le Li, Wanlong Xu, Yang Liu, Xinhui Wu, Haipeng Si, Kaidi Wang
pmc-13681885.description: Osteoarthritis (OA) is recognized as the most common chronic joint disease, characterized primarily by the degeneration of articular cartilage. Through screening a natural product library, we identified periplocin as a candidate agent capable of promoting chondrocyte anabolism. Periplocin, a cardiotonic steroid isolated from Periploca forrestii, has been proven to be involved in antiinflammatory responses.
